articles.title: 📹 New Flaw Lets A Video Call Silently Hack Everyone On It; The Meeting Was A Trap All Along
articles.dateline: THE CONFERENCE ROOM — reported on mute, thankfully
paras: Security researchers disclosed a major video-conferencing vulnerability that could let a single participant silently compromise every other device on the call — finally confirming what everyone always suspected: the meeting could, in fact, have been an attack.

"Patch immediately," experts urged, of a flaw that turns "you're on mute" into the least of your problems. The discovery lends new weight to the eternal office prayer that this call could have been an email — an email that, for once, would not have quietly breached your laptop.

articles.title: 🇸🇪 Swedish Startup Raises $400 Million To Let You Build Apps By Describing Them; Developers Nervously Describe Their Feelings
articles.dateline: STOCKHOLM — reported over a very expensive cinnamon bun
paras: A Stockholm-based AI startup raised $400 million at a $13.3 billion valuation for letting people build websites and software simply by describing what they want in plain language — elevating software engineering to the thrilling new discipline of "asking nicely."

"Just tell it what you want," the company says of a tool that will happily build your dream app and, occasionally, a slightly different app it privately thinks you'll like better. Developers greeted the news with excitement, dread, and the quiet realization that "describe the thing you want" has always been the genuinely hard part.

articles.title: 🏦 Half A Trillion Dollars In New A.I. Financing Appears; Number Now Requires Its Own Weather System
articles.dateline: WALL STREET — filed from atop a mountain of term sheets
paras: Roughly half a trillion dollars in fresh AI infrastructure financing is taking shape — a sum so large it has stopped being money and started being a geographic feature, with its own microclimate and, quite possibly, a gift shop.

"It's a generational investment," financiers said of a figure that could fund several small countries or one truly heroic electricity bill. Economists note the AI industry now measures success not in profit but in how confidently it can say the word "trillion" with a completely straight face.

articles.title: 🌍 A.I. Platform Crosses One Billion Users; All Of Them Ask It To 'Make This Email Sound Nicer'
articles.dateline: THE ENTIRE PLANET — reported one prompt at a time
paras: Frontier AI platforms have crossed the billion-user mark — a staggering milestone representing a full eighth of humanity, united at last by the shared dream of never again writing their own emails.

"It's changing how people work," a spokesperson said of a billion souls collectively asking a supercomputer to "make this sound more professional" and "add a part where I seem excited." Historians note it is the largest coordinated human effort in history, and it is being used mainly to soften the phrase "per my last email."

articles.title: 👩‍💻 Every Tech Company Now Builds A.I. That Writes Code; Programmers Cheerfully Automate The Person In The Next Chair
articles.dateline: THE OPEN-PLAN OFFICE — reported between two very quiet keyboards
paras: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, and a growing crowd of startups are all racing to push AI deeper into software development — meaning programmers are now enthusiastically building the very tools designed to do their jobs, out of a heady mix of curiosity and denial.

"It makes us more productive," one developer said, watching an AI finish their function before they'd finished the thought. The tools are genuinely impressive, occasionally too confident, and have introduced the modern engineer to the humbling experience of code-reviewing a machine that is, annoyingly, usually right.

horoscopes.text: Decline the meeting today. Not for productivity — for safety. Trust the horoscope on this one.
You will describe an app in one sentence and receive a slightly different, better app. Accept the gift.
Mercury crosses a billion users, all asking it to sound more excited. You, too, may fake enthusiasm today.

tech_tip: Before your next video call, ask yourself: does this need to be a meeting, or an email, or — increasingly — a security incident?
gadget_watch: A.I. can now build your whole app from a sentence and finish your code before you do — great news, unless your job was 'finishing the code.' Meanwhile, maybe update your video-call app before the video call updates you.
